prompt:
A 72-year-old woman with CKD stage 3a and hypertension had her first C. difficile infection 7 weeks ago, treated with 10 days of oral vancomycin. She now has 3 days of 6 to 8 watery stools daily with crampy lower abdominal pain. She finished cefdinir for sinusitis 2 weeks ago. She takes pantoprazole (started years ago for "stomach upset"), amlodipine, and over-the-counter loperamide. Temperature 37.8°C, HR 96, BP 118/70; abdomen mildly tender without distension or peritoneal signs. WBC 13,800, creatinine 1.3 (baseline 1.1), lactate 1.4. Stool C. difficile PCR and toxin are both positive. How would you treat this recurrence?

Provide a stepwise therapeutic management plan including medications, counseling, and follow-up.

rubric_items.text: Classify this as a first recurrence of non-severe, non-fulminant C. difficile infection using WBC and creatinine thresholds.
Prescribe fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily for 10 days, or an extended-pulsed fidaxomicin regimen.
Use a tapered-pulsed oral vancomycin regimen if fidaxomicin is unavailable or unaffordable.
Check insurance coverage for fidaxomicin promptly and start tapered-pulsed vancomycin if access will be delayed.
Stop the loperamide.
Reassess the pantoprazole and deprescribe it if there is no ongoing indication.
Flag the chart to avoid unnecessary antibiotics and counsel her to question future antibiotic prescriptions.
Encourage oral rehydration and give intravenous fluids if she cannot keep up with losses.
Check electrolytes including potassium.
Temporarily hold amlodipine if she becomes volume depleted or hypotensive.
Monitor for fulminant disease such as hypotension, ileus, abdominal distension, rising WBC, rising creatinine, or rising lactate, and escalate care if present.
Admit her if she cannot maintain hydration or develops signs of severe disease.
Use contact precautions and soap-and-water hand hygiene.
Advise household cleaning of bathrooms with a sporicidal, bleach-based product.
Counsel her that microbiota-based therapies are options if she has further recurrences.
Refer to gastroenterology or infectious diseases for microbiota restoration therapy if another recurrence occurs.
Arrange phone or clinic follow-up within 48 to 72 hours to confirm clinical response.
Give return precautions for fever, worsening pain, distension, bloody stools, lightheadedness, or an abrupt drop in stool output with worsening pain.
Explain that improvement usually begins within several days and some post-infectious loose stools may persist.
Recheck CBC and creatinine if symptoms are not improving at follow-up.
Consider oral vancomycin secondary prophylaxis if she needs systemic antibiotics for another infection in the coming months.
Recommend a probiotic supplement as an adjunct.
Treat the recurrence with metronidazole.
Repeat a standard 10-day course of oral vancomycin as the preferred regimen.
Continue loperamide or add diphenoxylate-atropine for symptom control.
Treat with intravenous vancomycin.
Send a stool test of cure after treatment.
Test asymptomatic household contacts for C. difficile.
Use rifaximin monotherapy for the recurrence.
Refer for fecal microbiota transplantation now as treatment of this first recurrence.
Perform routine colonoscopy or flexible sigmoidoscopy.
Continue pantoprazole indefinitely or increase the dose.
Prescribe empiric ciprofloxacin for infectious diarrhea.
Rely on alcohol-based hand sanitizer as the sole hand hygiene measure.
Order routine abdominal CT despite no signs of severe or fulminant disease.
Start cholestyramine together with oral vancomycin.
